newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar new declaration 20,000 tonnes this week.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar new declaration 20,000 tonnes this week.

text.p: About 20,000 tonnes of new declaration for Thai sugar were recorded this week, trade and shipping sources said on Thursday.
The new declaration involved orders from Japan, Maldives, and Singapore, the sources said.
The vessel Silver Song was expected to arrive at the Thai port on September 24 to load 17,650 tonnes of bulk raw sugar to be shipped to Japan. Kerry was said to be a buyer.

The vessel Sea Horse was scheduled to arrive between September 25-30 to load 1,500 tonnes of white sugar for shipment to Maldives. Gill & Duffus was a buyer. The loading would be cancelled if the ship failed to show up at the port during the specified period.
Another ship which would leave for Singapore with 800 tonnes of white sugar was scheduled to be ready by September 20.
Between September 10-20, about 40,000 tonnes of white and raw sugar were shipped or scheduled to be shipped to mostly Asian destinations, the sources said.
The vessel Pipob Samut was scheduled to leave Thai port on September 20 with 16,600 tonnes of bulk raw for Japan.
Another vessel, Akademik Pozdyunin, left the port on Friday with 3,000 tonnes of bagged white sugar, heading to Pakistan
